bodies.intuition: Data parallelism keeps a complete copy of the optimizer state on every worker, which is the same numbers stored N times. ZeRO shards them instead: each worker holds a slice, and the pieces are gathered when needed. The memory per worker falls almost linearly with the number of workers.
bodies.engineer: Three stages shard the optimizer state, then the gradients, then the parameters themselves. Each stage saves more memory and adds more communication, so the choice is a memory-for-bandwidth trade rather than a free win. Stage 3 makes models far larger than one device trainable without model parallelism.
bodies.math: With Ψ parameters, N workers and K bytes of optimizer state per parameter, memory per worker goes from 2Ψ + 2Ψ + KΨ to roughly 2Ψ + 2Ψ + KΨ/N at stage 1 and (2 + 2 + K)Ψ/N at stage 3.
